nary_nodes.label: War on Iran launched
evidence: Since the United States and Israel launched a war on Iran in late February

nary_nodes.label: Global energy sector upheaval
evidence: the global energy sector has undergone major upheaval

nary_nodes.label: Oil prices swinging
evidence: Oil prices have swung from levels not seen since the onset of Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022 to close to where they were before the conflict more than four months ago.

nary_nodes.label: Energy suppliers scramble for alternative routes
evidence: Energy suppliers have scrambled to find alternative trade routes amid Iran’s stranglehold over the Strait of Hormuz

nary_nodes.label: Governments roll emergency measures
evidence: governments have rolled emergency measures to spare citizens from the worst of the pain inflicted by surging fuel costs.

nary_nodes.label: US-Iran peace negotiations
evidence: ongoing US-Iran negotiations to reach a lasting peace

nary_nodes.label: Global energy landscape transformed
evidence: the war has already transformed the global energy landscape in ways that are likely to be long-lasting and even permanent

nary_nodes.label: Experts claim war transformed energy landscape
evidence: the war has already transformed the global energy landscape in ways that are likely to be long-lasting and even permanent, according to energy experts.

nary_nodes.label: Imsirovic claims oil market changed permanently
evidence: “The oil market will never be the same, following this conflict,” Adi Imsirovic, a veteran oil trader who lectures at the University of Oxford, told Al Jazeera.

nary_nodes.label: Imsirovic predicts new infrastructure and diversification
evidence: “New pipelines will urgently be built. New security arrangements will be put into place, and the buyers of oil from the region will look elsewhere for diversification,” Imsirovic said.

nary_nodes.label: Attacks on commercial vessels
evidence: Attacks on commercial vessels in the Strait of Hormuz

nary_nodes.label: Chilling effect on shipping lines expected
evidence: Attacks on commercial vessels in the Strait of Hormuz are widely expected to have a chilling effect on shipping lines that persists long after the war is officially brought to an end.

nary_nodes.label: Iran agrees to safe passage MoU
evidence: Iran agreed to make its “best efforts” to arrange the safe passage of vessels in the strait in the memorandum of understanding (MoU) signed with the US on June 17

nary_nodes.label: Iran claims right to control waterway
evidence: Tehran has since then repeatedly claimed the right to control the critical waterway.

nary_nodes.label: Maritime traffic drops
evidence: maritime traffic dropped sharply again over the weekend after attacks on two commercial ships that were widely blamed on Iran reignited fears for seafarers’ safety.

nary_nodes.label: Attacks blamed on Iran
evidence: attacks on two commercial ships that were widely blamed on Iran

nary_nodes.label: Energy suppliers seek land exports
evidence: energy suppliers have sought to ramp up exports on land via Saudi Arabia’s East-West Pipeline, the United Arab Emirates’ Abu Dhabi Crude Oil Pipeline, and the Iraq-Turkiye Crude Oil Pipeline

nary_nodes.label: Marks expects long-term transit concern
evidence: Dan Marks, a research fellow in energy security at the Royal United Services Institute in London, said he expects there to be “long-term” concern over transits in the strait.

nary_nodes.label: Marks claims strait closure possibility
evidence: “While the current Iranian regime remains in place and at odds with the United States and Israel, there will always be the possibility that tensions will flare and the strait will close,” Marks told Al Jazeera.

nary_nodes.label: Marks claims market weathered but investment impacted
evidence: “The global market has proven able to weather this for a relatively extended period, but it impacts appetite for investment into the region, where production and exports may be disrupted and tourists may be deterred.”

nary_nodes.label: Goh anticipates push to reduce strait reliance
evidence: June Goh, a Singapore-based senior oil market analyst at Sparta, a commodities data firm, said she anticipates a sustained push by energy producers and consumers alike to reduce their reliance on the strait.

nary_nodes.label: Goh explains producer strategy
evidence: “For the producers, this would come in the form of more pipeline evacuation routes from the Middle East,” Goh told Al Jazeera.

nary_nodes.label: Goh explains buyer strategy
evidence: “For the buyers, this would mean maintaining a healthy supply of strategic petroleum reserves.”

nary_nodes.label: Shift to renewables accelerates
evidence: Another anticipated legacy of the war is an acceleration in countries’ efforts to shift from fossil fuels to renewables, such as wind, solar and hydropower.

nary_nodes.label: Stiell claims conflict supercharging renewables boom
evidence: In April, Simon Stiell, the top United Nations climate official, told a meeting of government officials at the International Energy Agency that the conflict was already “supercharging the global renewables boom”.

nary_nodes.label: Global renewable energy capacity record high
evidence: Global renewable energy capacity hit a record high in 2025

nary_nodes.label: Non-fossil fuel projects share of added power capacity
evidence: non-fossil fuel projects accounting for approximately 86 percent of added power capacity that year

nary_nodes.label: Imsirovic predicts decline in ICE car sales
evidence: “Following this war, few people looking for a new car will opt for one with an internal combustion engine,” Oxford University’s Imsirovic said.

nary_nodes.label: Imsirovic predicts end of oil monopoly in road transport
evidence: “And this will finish the important monopoly of oil in road transportation,” Imsirovic said.

nary_nodes.label: Imsirovic claims air transport & petrochemicals minor oil demand
evidence: “What is left is the monopoly in air transport and petrochemicals, but that is a relatively minor volume of the overall demand.”

nary_nodes.label: Elheddad claims near-term fossil fuel stockpiling
evidence: While energy security imperatives are likely to lead many governments to stockpile fossil fuels in the near-term

nary_nodes.label: Elheddad claims strengthening economic case for renewables
evidence: the medium to long-term economic case for renewables will strengthen as geopolitical risk inflates “the true cost” of fossil fuel dependence

nary_nodes.label: Elheddad claims conflict may bring forward investment decisions
evidence: “The conflict may ultimately bring forward investment decisions that were already in motion,” Elheddad told Al Jazeera.

nary_nodes.label: China benefits from energy shift
evidence: China, more than any other country, stands to gain from an expedited global shift away from fossil fuels.

nary_nodes.label: China's share of renewable component production
evidence: The world’s second-largest economy is by far the top global exporter of renewable energy-related components, producing more than 80 percent of the world’s wind turbines, solar panels and energy storage batteries

nary_nodes.label: Obstfeld claims war shows value of diversified energy mix
evidence: The war has provided an “object lesson in the value of a much more diversified energy mix”, said Maurice Obstfeld, a senior fellow at the Peterson Institute for International Economics and a former chief economist at the International Monetary Fund.

nary_nodes.label: Obstfeld claims China will benefit
evidence: “China will benefit, given its dominance in providing renewable energy infrastructure products,” Obstfeld told Al Jazeera.

nary_nodes.label: Elheddad claims US & Qatar may consolidate supplier positions
evidence: Other countries such as the US and Qatar may also be able to consolidate their positions as leading energy suppliers in the aftermath of the war, said Elheddad, the University of Lancashire lecturer.

nary_nodes.label: Elheddad explains beneficiaries of energy economics
evidence: “From an energy economics perspective, the beneficiaries will be those with exportable surplus and stable supply guarantees,” Elheddad said.

nary_nodes.label: Elheddad claims US strengthens LNG supplier position
evidence: “The US strengthens its position as a swing LNG supplier.

nary_nodes.label: Elheddad claims Qatar consolidates contract partner role
evidence: Qatar consolidates its role as a reliable long-term contract partner.”

nary_nodes.label: Global oil & LNG supplies through Strait of Hormuz
evidence: about one-fifth of global oil and liquefied natural gas (LNG) supplies pass in peacetime.

nary_nodes.label: Post-war peak maritime transits
evidence: After hitting a post-war peak of more than 70 transits on June 24

nary_nodes.label: Pre-war oil volume through Strait
evidence: approximately 20 million barrels of oil that moved through the strait each day before the war.
